content:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 18d high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 18d moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.2), model underestimates mean reversion; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with 18d trend.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; apply 3x smoothing to final 5 days of forecast to reduce lag.
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive (e.g., >+0.2), model delays response; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment weight to forecast horizon.
